investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-24T21:46–21:53Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption was possible, leaving pods unscheduled for 135–144 seconds until the eval timeout was reached. No required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector and are therefore ineligible. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state and the agent VM is never created. This is a cluster-capacity or node-affinity configuration problem in the production-api runtime environment, not an eval infrastructure defect.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion: all allocatable VM slots on the 2 kata-peerpods-capable nodes are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or label drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not carry the required node label or affinity key, meaning effective scheduling capacity is structurally limited to only 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size.
TERTIARY — resource quota or limit range at the namespace level preventing new kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations even if node capacity were freed.
QUATERNARY — a recent workload surge or leaked/zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, preventing new allocations.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-24T21:46–21:53Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption was possible, leaving pods unscheduled for 135–144 seconds until the eval timeout was reached. No required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector and are therefore ineligible. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state and the agent VM is never created. This is a cluster-capacity or node-affinity configuration problem in the production-api runtime environment, not an eval infrastructure defect.

TERTIARY — resource quota or limit range at the namespace level preventing new kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations even if node capacity were freed.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Depleted Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-24 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: 0/6 nodes are available due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes and mismatched node affinity/selectors on the remaining 4. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any response evidence, leaving all required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes cluster resource constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that match the required node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector rules and preemption cannot help on any node. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 135–144 seconds before the probe timed out, preventing agent creation and making it impossible for the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1918: createAgent) to produce any evidence. The contract gap (missing orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is a downstream symptom of this upstream scheduling failure, not an independent code defect.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or a prior eval run consumed all available VM slots and they had not been released by the time the eval pods were submitted. All three sibling checks show the same error within a ~5-minute window (evidence: sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state, failed-check.message), consistent with sustained slot exhaustion rather than a transient spike.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node pool shrinkage: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, leaving only 2 nodes eligible. If the eligible node pool was recently reduced (e.g., scale-down, node failure, label change), the effective capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm slots would be lower than expected even if per-node limits are unchanged.

Tertiary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota or limit set too low for concurrent eval probes: if multiple eval runs or production workloads share the same VM slots, the quota may be insufficient to absorb simultaneous probe pods.
Lower confidence — a prior eval cleanup failure leaving orphaned remote-agent pods that continue to hold kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, preventing new pods from scheduling.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the production Kubernetes cluster immediately: run kubectl describe nodes and check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes to confirm whether slots are still exhausted.
Identify and, if safe, terminate any orphaned or stuck remote-agent pods that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without active workloads.

Review whether the node affinity/selector rules for remote-agent pods are intentionally restricting scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes; if the restriction is unintentional or if those 2 nodes are undersized, expand the eligible node pool or increase per-node VM slot capacity.
After restoring slot availability, re-run the eval probe (AURA_STATUS_RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT=production-api AURA_STATUS_CHECKS=remote-agent-runtime npm run status:probes) to confirm recovery.
Evaluate whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota is sufficient for concurrent eval probe runs plus production workloads; if not, increase the quota or stagger eval scheduling to avoid contention.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows that kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available and unallocated on the eligible nodes at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or admission controller issue should be investigated.

If the 4 nodes excluded by affinity/selector are shown to have been eligible in a prior passing run (i.e., their labels or taints changed recently), the root cause would shift toward a node pool configuration change rather than slot exhaustion.

If a re-run of the probe immediately after the failure succeeds without any cluster changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a concurrent workload briefly consumed all slots) rather than a sustained capacity problem.

If the remote-agent-create sibling check passes while remote-agent-runtime fails in isolation, the scheduling constraint is not uniformly blocking all remote-agent pod types and the affinity/selector configuration for the runtime pod specifically should be examined.

If no pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources are found running in the cluster at the time of failure, the resource accounting or quota configuration itself may be misconfigured rather than genuinely exhausted.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent pod creation, surfacing slot exhaustion as a distinct 'capacity' check status rather than a timeout failure.
Add an eval that monitors the count of currently running remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources, alerting when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold.
Add an eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector rules, alerting if the eligible node count drops below a minimum (e.g., below 3).

Consider a dedicated 'cluster-scheduling-health' eval for the remote-agents feature that validates both VM slot availability and node affinity eligibility independently of the end-to-end agent creation flow.
